title: Go: Schema Validator
description: Build a runtime schema validator in Go using struct tags and the reflect package for field-level validation.

steps.title: Field validation with struct tags
steps.description: Define struct tags for validation rules: `required`, `min`, `max`, `pattern`. Parse the `validate` tag in a `ValidateField` function using `reflect`. For a simple `User` struct with Name and Age fields, check that required fields are non-zero and numeric values respect min/max. Print validation results.
hints: Use `reflect.TypeOf(v).Field(i).Tag.Get("validate")` to extract the tag string
Parse tags: split by comma, then by '=' for parameterized rules like `min=18`
Use `reflect.ValueOf(v).Field(i).Interface()` to get the field value for comparison

verification.successMessage: Field validation correctly parses struct tags and validates fields!
verification.failureMessage: Print 'valid' for passing fields and 'invalid: <reason>' for failing fields.

steps.title: Reflect-based struct walker
steps.description: Implement a `WalkStruct` function that recursively walks all fields of a struct using `reflect`. Handle nested structs, pointers, and slices. For each field, print its name, type, kind, and value. Test with a struct containing nested fields and slices of structs.
hints: Use `reflect.ValueOf(v).Kind()` to handle different kinds recursively
For `reflect.Struct`, iterate fields; for `reflect.Ptr`, dereference with `.Elem()`
Print indented paths: `fmt.Printf("%s%s (%s)\n", indent, fieldName, fieldType)`

verification.successMessage: Reflect-based walker correctly traverses nested structs, pointers, and slices!
verification.failureMessage: Print each field's path, type, and kind from the struct traversal.

steps.title: Nested struct validation
steps.description: Extend the validator to validate nested structs recursively. When a field is a struct, slice of structs, or pointer to struct, descend into it and validate all sub-fields. Return a nested error map. Test with an `Address` struct nested inside a `Person` struct. Print the nested validation errors.
hints: Build a `ValidationErrors` type: `map[string]interface{}` where values can be nested maps
For nested structs, call `Validate` recursively and add result under the field name
For slices of structs, use index as key: `"addresses[0]"`

verification.successMessage: Nested struct validation correctly descends into sub-structs and slices!
verification.failureMessage: Print validation errors for nested fields showing the full path.

steps.title: Custom validators
steps.description: Implement a custom validator registration system. Define `type ValidatorFunc func(value interface{}, param string) bool` and a `RegisterValidator(name string, fn ValidatorFunc)` method. Support custom validators like `in=red,blue,green` and `regex=^[a-z]+$`. Register and test custom validators.
hints: Store registered validators in a `map[string]ValidatorFunc` on a `Validator` struct
The `in` validator checks if value is in a comma-separated list
The `regex` validator compiles the param as a `regexp.MustCompile(param)` and matches

verification.successMessage: Custom validators register and execute correctly alongside built-in rules!
verification.failureMessage: Print a valid and an invalid case using custom validators.

steps.title: Error aggregation and reporting
steps.description: Build an `ErrorAggregator` that collects all validation errors, de-duplicates them, and produces a formatted report. Support verbose and summary modes. Implement `AddError(field, message)`, `HasErrors()`, and `Report(verbose bool)`. Print both a summary and verbose report for a complex struct with multiple validation failures.
hints: Store errors as `map[string][]string` grouping by field path
Verbose report prints all errors grouped by field, summary prints just field count

verification.successMessage: Error aggregator produces clear, formatted validation reports!
verification.failureMessage: Print both a summary and verbose error report for the validation results.
